A module can own a core root name without rejection at registration time. The application boots successfully because the config is not read during registration. The InvalidConfigurationException surfaces later during boot() when AzGuardConfig resolves for the first time, preventing the app from serving traffic with a stolen core section.

AzGuardConfig::boot() resolves the config during boot. All module registrations finish before any boot method runs. Core register() binds a closure without resolving the config. A module cannot claim a core root after registration and before boot.

A module that registers after core and resolves AzGuardConfig would freeze the config before a later module claims a root. This is the documented "after frozen" error and is intentional.

The singletonIf bug remains the primary candidate. The code registers ConfigSections via singletonIf, then immediately resolves it to call own(). Laravel's singletonIf only binds when the abstract is not yet bound.

The upgrade document publishes an unsafe call pattern for application providers. Laravel registers package providers first, so that path is safe. The singletonIf bug cannot be fixed by simply resolving the class before binding, because Laravel never stored an unbound concrete instance in its instances map. The robust correction is a static registry inside ConfigSections that persists owners across all instances, eliminating any dependency on container identity.

A static registry would break test isolation because tests instantiate ConfigSections directly. The container singleton is the correct model. The fix is to check whether ConfigSections is already resolved or bound before calling singletonIf, then make and own.

That instance is discarded, so bound() remains false and the module's own() is already lost. The only robust fixes are to require modules to call singletonIf before make(), or to store owners in a static registry.
